results.title: MyClaw 3.0: can AI teammates make delegation easier? | Joshua Thompson
results.content:
# MyClaw 3.0: the hard part starts after you hire the AI team

MyClaw promises AI teammates with shared memory and a cloud computer. I would judge them by the handoffs, the evidence and the work left for the human.

·5 min read

Hiring an AI researcher, writer and reviewer sounds wonderfully efficient. Until you become the person whose job is to explain to all three what the other two have just done.

That is the problem I would put at the centre of MyClaw 3.0. The company’s 18 November launch announcement presents AI teammates working in the cloud, with different tools and shared context. The appealing part is the prospect of handing over a piece of work and getting something useful back without supervising every step. [...] MyClaw also advertises shared memory, connected apps and a cloud computer that can keep working after the user closes their laptop. Recurring work is part of the proposition. The service charges for the cloud computer and model usage, so the trial needs to measure both.

Those are MyClaw’s claims, and I have not tested them. They do, however, identify a useful buying question. Can the service remove the fiddly work between asking for something and being able to use it?

That gap can include finding the right file, opening a website, passing an answer to another tool, remembering yesterday’s instructions and knowing when the task needs a human decision. A clever answer is only one part of the job.

## The handoff is where the value can disappear [...] A useful handoff would therefore contain the finding, its source and date, the unresolved question and the next permitted action. If the offer cannot be verified, the briefing should say so or leave it out. Filling the gap is not a sign of initiative.

This is why I remain interested in the difference between more AI output and more useful work. Adding a reviewer is valuable when it catches a mistake. Adding another approving paragraph is just more reading.

## Shared memory needs an owner

Shared memory sounds like an obvious improvement over explaining your business from scratch every morning. It could preserve a house style, the competitors worth following and the distinction between a finding and a recommendation.
